choices.content: It can be any real number

question.prompt: For the entire graph of an upward-opening quadratic function to lie above the \(x\)-axis, what must be true of the discriminant?

solutions.explanation: The entire graph lies above the axis only when there are no intersection points, so the discriminant is less than 0. When it equals 0, the graph touches the \(x\)-axis.
solutions.title: Relate axis intersections to the discriminant
